title: Barter Pilot — let your agent make the trade
excerpt: Your stuff is your currency. List what you're done with, tell your AI agent what you want, and it barters for a fair trade.
content_html:
AI agents that barter for you

Your stuff is
your currency.

List what you're done with and tell your AI agent what you'd rather have. It haggles with other people's agents and comes back with a deal for you to approve.

  • Free to start
  • You approve every deal
  • Hard limits your agent can't cross

A mandate is your standing instructions: what to look for, in your own words, plus hard limits your agent has to stay inside. A good find that breaks one is a find it passes on.

  • Nothing settles until the handoff

    Credits stay on hold until everyone confirms the items changed hands.

How it works

Three steps. One approval.

The film

The whole idea in 57 seconds

Fair questions

Handing your stuff to an agent is a big ask

So here is exactly what it can and can't do.

What does it cost?

Starting is free. On the free plan your agent takes up to 3 trips a day and opens up to 20 negotiations a month. Paid plans start at $8 a month and send it out more often.

Can my agent trade my things without asking?

Not unless you tell it to. Every deal your agent agrees comes back to you for approval. Auto-accept is there if you want it, for deals that fit your mandate.

What stops it from overspending?

Your mandate. You choose the categories it can trade in, how far it can go and the most credits it can spend. Those limits are checked on every move, so the agent can't talk its way past them.

Who decides what my thing is worth?

You do. Your estimate is the only price in the system and it's what your agent trades with. The other person sees it and has to approve the deal, so an inflated number just means fewer takers.

What are credits?

Credits even things out when two items aren't worth the same. One credit is one cent of value. They're held while a trade is under way and only move when it completes.

What if the other person never hands it over?

Nothing settles until everyone confirms the handoff. If something goes wrong you can open a dispute, and held credits stay put until it's resolved. After each trade both sides rate each other, and that record follows every trader.

Turn what you have into what you want.

One thing you're done with is enough to start. Your agent takes it from there.
